Title: Incident venous thromboembolic events in the Prospective Study of Pravastatin in the Elderly at Risk (PROSPER)
Author: Freeman et al.
Comment: No separate DVT count was reported; definite VTE was substituted exactly as defined by the paper. The analyzed denominators exclude participants using warfarin at baseline and are smaller than the 5804 originally randomized. PROSPER included participants with either established vascular disease or vascular risk factors, so the cohort was not exclusively primary prevention. The paper reported an HR, not an OR; the requested statin-versus-placebo OR should be calculated downstream from the extracted 2×2 counts.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Pravastatin 40 mg/day') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False); excluded by outcome classification: does not match the requested outcome/timepoint (meta_analysis_candidate=False)
Design Type: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled parallel-group trial; pre-planned post hoc VTE analysis
domain: Venous thromboembolism prevention with statin therapy
Participant type: Men and women aged 70–82 with pre-existing vascular disease or at least one major vascular risk factor
Outcome measurement: Definite VTE adjudicated from full medical records by clinicians; confirmation required death certificate evidence or recorded objective testing, with consensus of two clinical opinions
Outcome variable: Definite incident venous thromboembolism (VTE; used because no separate DVT count was reported)
effect_direction: OR < 1 favors statin; observed events were more frequent with pravastatin than placebo.

Author: Glynn et al.
Comment: The paper reports a hazard ratio, not an odds ratio. The raw participant counts (17/8901 vs 38/8901) are extracted for downstream calculation of the requested statin-versus-placebo OR. Design Type: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter parallel-group trial
Participant type: Apparently healthy adult men aged 50 years or older and women aged 60 years or older without prior cardiovascular disease
Outcome measurement: First clinically symptomatic deep-vein thrombosis; site confirmation sources included venous ultrasonogram or venogram
effect_direction: OR < 1 favors statin; observed events were less frequent with rosuvastatin than placebo.

Report_ID: Adjudicated venous thromboembolism (VTE) at 90-day follow-up (eligible DVT proxy; no separate DVT count reported)
Title: Atorvastatin versus Placebo in ICU Patients with COVID-19: Ninety-day Results of the INSPIRATION-S Trial
Author: Talasaz et al.
Comment: No separate DVT count was reported, so the paper’s adjudicated VTE participant count was used exactly as the eligible proxy. Per the synthesis contract, denominators are the numbers randomized (303 atorvastatin; 302 placebo), although Table 1’s prespecified primary analysis population was smaller (290 and 297) and supplied the displayed percentages. Consequently, the reported percentages do not equal the event counts divided by the randomized denominators. The paper reports a hazard ratio, not the requested odds ratio; no OR was invented or calculated in this extraction row. The trial population consisted of critically ill ICU patients with COVID-19 rather than a general community primary-prevention population.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Atorvastatin 20 mg once daily') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Design Type: Double-blind multicenter randomized placebo-controlled trial with 2×2 factorial design
domain: Clinical medicine; COVID-19; venous thromboembolism prevention
Study Environment: Intensive care units in a multicenter trial
Medium: Atorvastatin 20 mg tablet or matching placebo
Content length: Intended treatment through 30 days from enrollment or until reaching the 30-day primary efficacy outcome; outcome follow-up through 90 days
Topic of Content: Primary prevention of thrombotic complications in critically ill adults with COVID-19
interaction_type: Blinded pharmacologic treatment versus matching placebo
Participant type: Adults with PCR-confirmed COVID-19 admitted to an ICU, excluding those with a strong indication for or ongoing use of statins
Outcome measurement: Number of participants with adjudicated, imaging-confirmed venous thromboembolism by 90 days
Outcome variable: Adjudicated venous thromboembolism (VTE) at 90-day follow-up (eligible DVT proxy; no separate DVT count reported)
effect_direction: OR < 1 favors statin; observed events were less frequent with atorvastatin than placebo.
